blocks: In Ableton's software and instruments, a clip is one piece of musical material on a track, such as a melody, a drum pattern, a bassline or a whole song. Ableton/Live, Ableton/Note, Move and Push all play clips.
A clip comes in two kinds, and each plays only on a track of its own kind:
Ableton/Clip/Audio — plays part of a sample on an audio track.
A clip comes in two kinds, and each plays only on a track of its own kind:
Ableton/Clip/MIDI — holds notes and controller envelopes and plays on a MIDI track.
A clip comes in two kinds, and each plays only on a track of its own kind:

A clip sits in a slot of the Session View, where its own launch button starts it, or on the timeline of the Arrangement View. A track plays one clip at a time (Ableton/Live/UG/03 Live Concepts/06 Arrangement and Session, Ableton/Live/UG/03 Live Concepts/07 Tracks).
The Clip View edits one clip's properties, such as its start and end, looping and launch settings. In the Session View, a clip's Follow Actions decide which clip plays after it.
A Live Clip, an Ableton/File/.alc file, saves one clip for reuse (Ableton/Live/UG/05 Managing Files and Sets/03 Live Clips).

In Ableton/Live, an audio clip is a clip that points to a sample, a sound file such as a WAV or an MP3, and says which part of it to play and how (Ableton/Live/UG/03 Live Concepts/09 Audio Clips and Samples).
It plays on an audio track. Dragging a sample in from the browser, or recording on an audio track, creates one.
Its settings in the Clip View change playback without altering the sample file.
Warping changes its playback speed independently of its pitch, so it follows the Set's tempo (Ableton/Live/UG/09 Audio Clips Tempo and Warping).
